description:
## Goal

Quiescent finality follows one derivation's exact ownership, not whichever single output a consumer happened to ask about first.

## Evidence and blocker

fz-kdt.57 removes root-wide transport relation authorities and publishes exact IncomingInputSlot contributions from existing RuntimeDemand derivations. Operator-reference semantic outputs remain byte-identical, but ordinary product driving now needs 38 quiescence events versus 32 before, exceeding the existing 34-event ceiling. The first 31 events are identical; six extra late events settle individual InputSlot claims whose owning RuntimeDemand derivations have already had a co-output arbitrated. Direct fact consumption and exact slot/shape prerequisite batching do not remove these rounds.

Scheduler::settle_quiescent_fact currently clears unfinal publishers only on the requested fact. Publisher identity is (Job, DerivationId), which already owns the exact reads and outputs. Claiming one clean conclusion's outputs have unrelated finality creates repeated arbitration, not new semantic work.

Baseline traces: /tmp/fz-tfn12-trace.36fmrk/00181.jsonl and /tmp/fz-kdt57-artifact-baseline.Et4zBB/operator.collapsed.jsonl. The independent regression must reproduce this on the generic scheduler without depending on .57 source facts.

## Strategy and signal

Start with a minimal RED generic scheduler test: one derivation publishes two outputs over quiescent cyclic ground, and arbitrating one leaves the same derivation's sibling claim unfinal. Resolve the precise ownership model before changing implementation. If arbitration certifies a derivation, publish finality for that exact derivation's owned claims through ordinary propagation. Never certify another derivation of the same job, another publisher, a dirty claim, or a derivation grounded in an unsettled external product.

Use the existing publisher output frontier and readiness movement path, semantic ordering and idempotent coalescing. No global scan, second registry, private cone, blanket certification, new fixpoint loop or telemetry suppression.

## Required finality accounting

The RED co-output test proves that certifying one output leaves its sibling unfinal on the old implementation. A first candidate that reset the unfinal-read count to zero is unsound: after licensing an old unquiet input B, a new quiet-to-unquiet input A increments the count, then B becoming quiet can cancel A's outstanding dependency.

Retain the real unquiet-read count in the existing per-derivation finality authority. Distinguish pending from quiescent-certified state explicitly; quiet movement decrements the real count, while a new unquiet edge revokes the certificate. A formula recompletion recounts its actual reads. Do not introduce a second registry or recompute upstream cones. Pin the mixed old/new dependency ordering RED/GREEN and verify the certificate cannot hide an unsettled external product.

## Acceptance

- One arbitration settles exact concordant claims once; subsequent asks do no arbitration work.
- A separate dirty/unfinal derivation and an independent second publisher remain authoritative and unfinal.
- Unsettled external product ground blocks certification; unrelated external products do not.
- Later content/readiness movement unfinalizes exact dependents normally; equal reproductions retain generations and do not wake Current readers.
- Fact values/revisions are unchanged by arbitration; all readiness transitions and exact wakes remain present in causal telemetry.
- Semantic answers and artifacts stay identical; deterministic work ceilings are unchanged or tighter.
- Generic scheduler/derivation/external-ground tests, retained macro/product tests, full library, serial fixture matrix, CLI causal/artifact tests, fmt/check/strict clippy pass.
- Update fact-engine/northstar guidance with the actual derivation-level rule. This bounded ownership correction does not claim fz-kdt.46's remaining edge-triggered drain-scan cutover is complete.

Deliver independently before fz-kdt.57: implementation by subagent, ticket-scoped cold review, one commit and close. Preserve the uncommitted .57 work without folding it into this commit.

## Standalone verification evidence

The exact operator-reference trace has 14 quiescence rounds versus 32 at fz-tfn.12; the 34-round ceiling is not raised. Formula evaluations fall 361 to 350: DeriveExecutableFacts falls 30 to 18; DeriveRuntimeDemand rises 41 to 42 because function 178/arrow 116 separately consumes moved RuntimeDemandInputs from functions 179 and 158 rather than coalescing both wakes. All other formula-family counts are unchanged; every evaluation remains causally attributed. Product settlement/generation counts remain 398, with 16 cache hits and no displacements. The full CLI causal test passes with these exact counts. The initial full library run had 1840 passes, two old work-count assertion failures, and six preexisting ignored tests. Both failed tests now pass independently: retained roots evaluate each distinct executable once (two root-owned leaf keys plus their callers), with exact causal closure checks preserved; take/drop total evaluations fall 4489 to 4233, exactly 263 fewer ExecutableFacts readiness resumes offset by seven additional Current RuntimeDemandInputs-caused resumes. All other formula families, blocked work and 311 demanded keys are unchanged. Final serial library passes 1842 tests with zero failures and six preexisting ignores. Serial fixture matrix passes531/531; full CLI passes30/30, with the simplified exact cause assertion rerun green. Normal commit hooks pass formatting, workspace check, and strict all-target clippy. Cold review approved production finality, CLI causality, and the final library-test supplement. Delivered independently in commit acb54dd81; the primary branch preserves uncommitted fz-kdt.57 work.
